How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide on how to **generate and execute a RESTful API request** for the “Get information of device connector versions” endpoint in **Cisco Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1**. I’ll cover both the **web‑UI (API Explorer)** and a **command‑line/Postman** approach so you can pick the one that fits your workflow. --- ## 1. Understand the Endpoint | Item | Value | |------|-------| | **API Name** | Get information of device connector versions | | **HTTP Method** | `GET` | | **Base URL** | `https:///api/v1` (replace `` with your Nexus Dashboard FQDN/IP) | | **Full Path** | `/api/v1/device-connector-versions` | | **Query Parameters** | None (unless you need filtering – see below) | | **Headers** | `Authorization: Bearer ` (or Basic Auth)
`Accept: application/json` | | **Response** | JSON array of connector‑version objects | > **Tip:** If you need to filter by device, connector type, or status, check the API docs for optional query parameters such as `deviceId`, `connectorType`, etc. --- ## 2. Using the Nexus Dashboard UI (API Explorer) 1. **Log in** to the Nexus Dashboard web console. 2. Click the **“API”** tab (usually located in the top‑right corner or under the “Developer” menu). 3. In the **API Explorer** pane, locate the endpoint named **“Get information of device connector versions”**. 4. Click the endpoint to expand its details. 5. Click **“Try it out”** (or similar button). 6. If the endpoint accepts query parameters, fill them in. 7. Click **“Execute”**. 8. The response will appear in the lower pane. 9. You can copy the generated request (method, URL, headers) for use in scripts or Postman. > **Screenshot**: > ![API Explorer](https://example.com/api-explorer.png) *(replace with actual screenshot if available)* --- ## 3. Using cURL (Command Line) ```bash # Replace with your Nexus Dashboard hostname/IP # Replace with a valid JWT or Basic Auth credentials curl -X GET \ "https:///api/v1/device-connector-versions" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ --insecure # remove if you have a valid cert ``` ### Optional Query Parameters If you want to filter results: ```bash curl -X GET \ "https:///api/v1/device-connector-versions?deviceId=12345&connectorType=ethernet" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Accept: application/json" ``` --- ## 4. Using Postman 1. **Create a new request**. 2. Set **Method** to `GET`. 3. Enter the URL: `https:///api/v1/device-connector-versions`. 4. Under **Headers**, add: - `Authorization: Bearer ` - `Accept: application/json` 5. (Optional) Add query parameters in the **Params** tab. 6. Click **Send**. 7. Inspect the **Body** tab for the JSON response. --- ## 5. Authentication Options | Method | How to obtain | Example Header | |--------|---------------|----------------| | **Bearer Token** | Use the “Generate Token” feature in the dashboard or via the `/auth/token` endpoint. | `Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...` | | **Basic Auth** | Username/password of a dashboard user. | `Authorization: Basic dXNlcjpwYXNz` | | **Client Certificate** | If your organization uses mutual TLS. | `--cert client.pem --key client.key` (cURL) | > **Security Note:** Always use HTTPS. If you’re running the command locally, consider adding `--cacert /path/to/ca.pem` to verify the server certificate. --- ## 6. Sample Response ```json [ { "connectorId": "eth0", "deviceId": "router-01", "version": "v1.2.3", "status": "active", "lastUpdated": "2024-10-18T12:34:56Z" }, { "connectorId": "eth1", "deviceId": "router-01", "version": "v1.2.3", "status": "active", "lastUpdated": "2024-10-18T12:34:56Z" } ] ``` --- ## 7. Troubleshooting | Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix | |---------|--------------|-----| | **401 Unauthorized** | Token expired or wrong | Refresh token or re‑authenticate | | **404 Not Found** | Wrong base URL or endpoint path | Verify the host and `/api/v1/device-connector-versions` | | **500 Internal Server Error** | Backend issue | Check Nexus Dashboard logs or contact support | | **SSL Error** | Self‑signed cert | Add `--insecure` (cURL) or import CA cert | --- ## 8. Next Steps 1. **Automate**: Wrap the cURL command in a shell script or use a language SDK (Python `requests`, Go `net/http`, etc.). 2. **Schedule**: Use cron or a CI/CD pipeline to poll connector versions periodically. 3. **Integrate**: Feed the data into a monitoring dashboard or alerting system. --- ### Quick Reference (cURL) ```bash curl -X GET \ "https:///api/v1/device-connector-versions" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ --insecure ``` Replace placeholders with your actual values. That’s it—your RESTful request is ready!
